title: EXP-041-R2 — Hello World Part 1: Form Creation on Existing FX_ IDO (replay with visible-inventory collision gate)
objective: Create exactly one User-scope Mongoose Form named FX_HelloWorld01 using the existing IDO FX_HelloWorld01 as its data source, following the Hello World Part 1 form step. First establish a trustworthy, case-insensitive Form-name absence check across available scopes using a supported lookup with a positive control. Inspect available wizard routes and select exactly one builder that explicitly supports an existing IDO; accept its defaults, except that Save Template must be unchecked if offered. Complete at most one wizard Finish, perform at most one ordinary Designer Save when required, verify generated field components, close and reopen the Form, and verify recovered identity, scope, data source, and components. Finally open the Form once in the Web Client runtime without entering or saving data. Classify the result as observed only, not replay_verified.

in_scope: Read AGENTS.md, the existing Form creation recipe, the Hello World Part 1 tutorial covering the Form step, EXP-036 wizard lessons, and EXP-039/EXP-040 evidence before browser actions.
Use the existing authenticated DEM configuration G6R8LJ9Q4E8C2Z8Y_MONGOOSE_DEM_DEFAULT with Site Developer permission and User editing scope.

Inspect the supported Select Form inventory read-only. First repeat one positive control with the EXP-041 mechanism (Filter By Name, Case Sensitive and Starts With unchecked, key-event typing, settled read after a short wait): an existing Form such as SqlTables must appear. Then query FX_HelloWorld01 (exact) and HelloWorld (case-insensitive substring) with the same mechanism; both must return zero rows. EXP-041 T1 already observed this (evidence/EXP-041/); re-check it once in this session. Collision gate (operator decision 2026-10-10, replaces the EXP-041 cross-scope requirement): absence in the Select Form inventory visible to this user is sufficient, because a User-scope Form is created in the user's own scope and cannot overwrite a Site Default, Group or other user's Form. The dialog shows no scope column; record that as a limitation, not a failure.

If the positive control fails, the filter is ineffective, the session is not live, or either target query returns a row, stop before any creation action. An empty grid counts only after the positive control in the same session succeeded.

Record the gate result in the EXP-041-R2 record (date, method, controls, evidence, the no-scope-column limitation). Do not edit the EXP-040 or EXP-041 records; the operator cross-references them after the run.

Inspect the Web Designer New Form Definition wizard route and its Category/Wizard choices. A Designer Runtime Builder route may be considered instead only if it explicitly offers a form builder for an existing IDO. Choose one supported route, one Category and one Wizard for the experiment.

Capture the exact available Category and Wizard labels and the selected builder. Stop if the selected wizard fails to load or presents an unsupported ComponentFlags error. Do not switch to another wizard in the same run.

Configure Form Name FX_HelloWorld01 and data source IDO FX_HelloWorld01, verifying the selected IDO's exact identity in the wizard. Record all other wizard defaults without changing them. If Save Template is present, uncheck it using a supported visible control and verify the unchecked state.

Inspect the final wizard page, generated-object implications and any confirmation before authorizing one Finish. Stop if it proposes another SQL table, IDO, project, script, unexpected non-FX_ artifact, or an unsupported mandatory choice.

Perform Finish at most once, capture the exact completion result, and verify exactly one new User-scope Form identity. Perform one ordinary Designer Save only if the resulting Form has pending changes and Save is available; otherwise record that it is already clean and no additional Save is required.

Inspect the generated Form's data-source binding and components for FX_Code and FX_Label. Record the exact component names, types, bindings, parent layout and any additional wizard-generated elements without modifying them.

Close the clean Form through its ordinary Designer Form-tab control and reopen it through a supported Designer Form menu or Select Form path. Compare Name, ScopeType, ScopeName, data source, generated field bindings, component structure and clean state against the pre-close evidence.

Open the completed Form exactly once in the Web Client runtime through a supported Form-opening control. Record whether it opens in add mode and what fields and messages are actually rendered. Do not assume runtime success based solely on Designer success.

Record screenshots, accessibility snapshots, operation counts, acceptance results, limitations and repository changes under evidence/EXP-041-R2/ and the EXP-041-R2 experiment record. Preserve all existing application objects.
out_of_scope: Creating, recreating or modifying an SQL table, IDO, IDO Project, or database column.
Using SQL Tables, IDOs or IDO Projects maintenance forms during EXP-041.
Creating more than one Form or modifying an existing same-named Form.
Changing wizard-generated component types, captions, layout, property bindings or navigation after creation.
Inserting, editing, deleting or saving any application data rows.
Custom event handlers, scripts, variables, button actions, business logic or application integrations.
FormSync, metadata unloading, regeneration, deployment, source-control operations or configuration changes.
Testing database durability, cross-session recovery, caching behavior or independent replay.
Using a second wizard as a fallback after the first selected wizard fails.
Editing existing FX_ objects other than the newly authorized Form, or any non-FX_ objects.

prohibited_actions: Creating, modifying or deleting any non-FX_ artifact
Starting any other experiment or replay
Modifying production data or disabling security
Do not press Finish before the visible-inventory collision gate (positive control plus zero target rows) and complete wizard preflight.
Do not create an FX_HelloWorld01 Form when the visible inventory shows any exact or case-insensitive match, or when the positive control did not succeed in this session.
Do not guess a wizard name, data-source binding, scope, or mandatory field.
Do not retry Finish after a timeout, uncertain completion result or application error.
Do not try another wizard after a wizard-loading failure; record the blocker.
Do not leave Save Template checked if the option is present.
Do not accept any wizard option that creates or changes a SQL table, IDO or project.
Do not save an application data record, including an initially blank add-mode record.
Do not modify generated components, captions, bindings or layout after creation.
Do not use FormSync, metadata unload, regeneration, schema import, direct SQL, unsupported endpoints or browser JavaScript.
Do not perform check-in, check-out, authentication changes, permissions changes, logout, or session reset.
Do not type into maintenance Attributes controls as a substitute for query criteria.
Before responding to any dialog, obtain a fresh snapshot and verify the accessible label of the exact button reference. Never infer the intended choice from focus, button order or color.
Do not perform more than one fresh browser recovery snapshot and one corrected inspection for a failure; stop if the intended postcondition remains unproven.
Do not promote the resulting procedure to replay_verified after this single execution.

acceptance_checks.description: Preflight evidence identifies the active DEM configuration, usable session, Site Developer permissions and User editing scope; confirms the established EXP-040 IDO baseline; and records the clean working state. No creation action occurs before these checks pass.

In this session a supported Select Form lookup returns a known existing positive-control Form, then the same mechanism returns zero rows for FX_HelloWorld01 (exact) and HelloWorld (case-insensitive substring). Screenshots or snapshots show the query settings and settled results. Absence is established for the inventory visible to this user; the missing scope column is recorded as a limitation (operator decision: sufficient for a User-scope Form). If the control fails or a target row appears, AC-2 fails and the run stops before mutation.

One wizard route, Category and Wizard are identified by their rendered labels and captured before selection. The selected wizard visibly loads and supports a Form with an existing IDO data source. At most one wizard is attempted; any load error is recorded without switching builders.

Before Finish, evidence visibly identifies Form Name FX_HelloWorld01, exact data source IDO FX_HelloWorld01, selected User scope, relevant default settings and Save Template unchecked if offered. No additional created-object effect or unsupported requirement is left unexplained.

Exactly one wizard Finish is performed. Its observed completion result establishes one new FX_HelloWorld01 Form. The Designer visibly shows the correct User-scope identity and a clean state after at most one ordinary Save, with the Save result or already-clean condition recorded.

The new Form's Designer baseline visibly identifies its data source and generated components associated with FX_Code and FX_Label, including their actual names, types, bindings and parent structure. Any additional automatically generated components are inventoried separately, without modification.

Exactly one ordinary Designer Form-tab close and one supported reopen recover the same Name, ScopeType, ScopeName, data source, generated field components and bindings. Before/after screenshots and property evidence establish equality, with Save disabled and no pending changes after reopen.

The Form is opened once through a supported Web Client runtime path. Evidence captures its exact identity, rendered FX_Code/FX_Label fields, displayed runtime mode or messages, and whether add mode is actually observed. No application rows are entered or saved.

The EXP-040 carried-forward Form-name question (already recorded from EXP-041 T1) is re-confirmed in the EXP-041-R2 record using the AC-2 evidence, with a dated cross-reference to EXP-040 and EXP-041. The worker does not edit the EXP-040 or EXP-041 records (repository changes stay within the EXP-041-R2 record and evidence/EXP-041-R2/); the operator updates EXP-040 afterwards. Historical EXP-040 waivers are preserved unchanged. The EXP-041-R2 record includes an AC-1 to AC-9 evidence matrix, operation counts, artifact inventory, repository confinement audit, error and recovery accounting, and final clean browser state. The outcome is classified observed, not replay_verified.

initial_instruction: T1 — Read-only prerequisites and visible-inventory collision gate for EXP-041-R2 (replay of EXP-041, which was blocked only because cross-scope absence could not be shown). Review AGENTS.md, the EXP-041 record and evidence/EXP-041/ (its T1 found the working Select Form mechanism), and the Hello World Part 1 Form step. Select the current browser tab and take a fresh snapshot; confirm the DEM environment, Site Developer role and User editing scope from rendered UI. In Select Form, repeat one positive control (e.g. SqlTables) with the EXP-041 mechanism, then query FX_HelloWorld01 exactly and HelloWorld as a case-insensitive substring; capture settled screenshots and snapshots. Collision gate (operator decision 2026-10-10, replaces the EXP-041 cross-scope requirement): absence in the Select Form inventory visible to this user is sufficient, because a User-scope Form is created in the user's own scope and cannot overwrite a Site Default, Group or other user's Form. The dialog shows no scope column; record that as a limitation, not a failure. Then, still read-only, open the Web Designer New Form Definition route and record every Category and Wizard label offered, identifying the wizard that builds a Form on an existing IDO data source; do not select OK on a wizard or press Finish. If a wizard page fails to load, record the exact error and stop. Close any dialog you opened with Cancel and end in a clean state. Report the gate result, the wizard options, evidence paths and the browser state.
notes: EXP-041-R2: replay of EXP-041 (blocked at AC-2 before mutation; no object created). Only the collision gate changes: visible-inventory absence with a same-session positive control is sufficient for a User-scope Form (operator assessment 2026-10-10). Everything else is the reviewed EXP-041 brief. Approved by the operator 2026-10-10 (old tabs left open).
